$schema_note: Hand-curated record of the numbers recorded about what a monster's rank (enemyRarity 1-4) does to it, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/monster_rank_model.py never reads it; tests/test_monster_rank_model.py reads both and checks that the model reproduces each entry, and that each of the model's four boss hypotheses (health, damage, XP, drop rank) stays None until a `measured` entry names that dimension (the words health, damage, XP or drop rank in `what`) and an object descending from Enemy_Child_Boss_obj, and carries `values.ratio`, and carries no `confounds` (nothing but the rank changed on that boss, or what else changed, the Bosses control's affix top-up in `values.affixes_written`, was matched by the same session's identity control, which `values.controlled_by` names: an ordinary monster the Monster Rarity sliders raised with the same top-up, measured `pass` on that dimension), and is then the bool that ratio gives (within the identity control's tolerance of the rank table's ratio follows it: 10% for damage, 2% for XP, 5% for health, which has no control; the drop rank follows when the first DropItem argument is the rank written). A row with `confounds` decides no hypothesis, however its ratio compares: it stays a measurement of what the feature did, not of the game's rank scaling for a boss alone. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/monster-rank-spec.md. Every entry has `id` (MK1, MK2, ...), `kind` (`baseline` = vanilla, no lever; `target` = a ForgePact lever applied; `our_code` = a contract of ForgePact's own code, not the game), `status` (`measured`, `reported` = a player's report, not a measurement of ours, `qualitative`, `approximate`, `not_observed` or `our_code`), `date` (the measurement date, or the date a report was recorded), `source` (a list of {path, section} or {repo, commit}; paths are relative to the hub root, `section` is text that appears in that file), `scripts` (every `gml_Script_*` the entry involves, all bound in hs_game_sdk.scripts.GameScript), `what` (the observation; the word boss appears only in an entry about a boss), `values`, `model` (what the model must show), optionally `confounds` (a list: what else changed on the boss besides its rank, or what keeps the sample from deciding anything) and exactly one of `reproduced_by` (the dotted id of the test that reproduces it) or `not_reproduced` (why it cannot be). MK1-MK4 are AFK FARM's ordinary monsters (6,471 packets, 214 capture sessions, 2026-09-17 to 09-24, game builds pe6aaa6779 and pe6a9ed3ee). MK6-MK14 are ForgePact#44's Live procedure 1 (rerun of 2026-10-02, research DLL f85bc1d5...289cf, Nightmare, Outskirts of Inoya, zone level 170, every boss spawned with instance_create_depth and killed by writing its protected health to 0); the session's checks and their verdicts are in ForgePact/docs/boss-rarity-research.md, Live procedure 1. MK15-MK24 are ForgePact#44's Live procedure 1b (2026-10-02, research DLL 6c6dfd8e...63cb09, the same zone and difficulty, the same spawn and kill routes; capture .claude/workorders/forgepact-issue-44-uber-bosses-live-1b.md, hub, local): MK15-MK18 are its identity control on an ordinary Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj, which proved `damage` and `killExperience` against MK1 on the probe's own read path, and MK19-MK24 the Karp King at rank 1 and raised to rank 4; the session's record is ForgePact/docs/boss-rarity-research.md, Live procedure 1b. A value the research probe printed as `->?` (a number read as if it were a protected-store key, the key unproven) is kept under `unproven_reads` and is never evidence on its own; in Live 1b the same `->?` reads of `damage` and `killExperience` count only because the identity control (MK15, MK16) showed, on the same instrument, that they move with an ordinary monster's rank by MK1's ratios.

source.section: From AFK FARM's 6,471 recorded packets and 214 capture sessions

measurements.what: Rank multipliers next to the same monster object at rank 1 in the same room, medians over 41-48 pairs: health x1.84, x2.98, x4.23; damage x1.27, x1.53, x1.90; XP x2.75, x4.25, x6.25 for ranks 2, 3 and 4. The XP multipliers are exact constants.
measurements.model: RANK_TABLE[rank].hp, .damage and .xp equal these values exactly, and scaled(rank, ...) multiplies the rank-1 bases by them.

source.section: From AFK FARM's 6,471 recorded packets and 214 capture sessions

measurements.what: Protected drop values by rank, identical within a rank: dCommonChance 4/20/36/50, dCommonDropMult 11/20/42/58, dSatanicDropMult 1/0.925/0.475/0.285, dSlots 1, 1-3, 2-5, 4-8 for ranks 1-4. DropItem's first argument equals the rank in every packet.
measurements.model: RANK_TABLE[rank]'s common_chance, common_drop_mult, satanic_drop_mult and slots equal these values exactly.

source.section: From AFK FARM's 6,471 recorded packets and 214 capture sessions

measurements.what: The monster's drop table rises with rank: runes (drop type 4) 12/22/34/100 and dungeon keys (type 12) 5/40/75/100 for ranks 1-4.
measurements.model: Not modelled: the model carries the protected drop values, not the monster's drop table.
measurements.not_reproduced: The drop table is per monster and per drop type; these are two examples, not a rule the model could state. Recorded so a boss's drop table can be compared with them.

source.section: From AFK FARM's 6,471 recorded packets and 214 capture sessions

measurements.what: Kill mix by rank: without ForgePact's rarity sliders 70.1/16.9/10.4/0.1 % of 2,994 kills at ranks 1-4; with the sliders on, 35.1/18.9/32.1/13.8 % of 21,122 kills.
measurements.model: Not modelled: the model draws no random number, and the mix is the spawner's roll (and the sliders'), which it does not cover.
measurements.not_reproduced: The kill mix is a spawn-time roll, outside EnemyRaritySettings' arithmetic, and the model is deterministic.

measurements.what: A player's report on ForgePact v1.4.1: with the Monster Rarity sliders at 20% rare and 20% ancient, an Anubis boss went from about 500k to about 4.5M HP.
measurements.model: None: a report sets no hypothesis. Its ratio (about x9) is above every health multiplier in MK1.
measurements.not_reproduced: A report, not a measurement of ours: the boss's rank, its rank-1 base and how the numbers were read are unknown. It is why the sliders leave bosses alone, not evidence about whether a boss follows the rank table.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj, a boss, unraised (Bosses control off; the game's own setup traced at enemyRarity 1): health 44,625,000 on two separate spawns, read through the protected-store getter the probe's control proved (baseline-karp pass).

values.zone: Nightmare, Outskirts of Inoya, zone level 170

measurements.model: scaled(1, 44625000, ...) returns the health unchanged; MK7's rank-1 value is this one.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj, a boss, raised to rank 4 by ForgePact's Bosses control, with that control's 3-affix top-up (16 Multishot, 17 Treasure Gobbler, 25 Pyromaniac): health 252,242,812 against 44,625,000 at rank 1 in the same zone (MK6), a ratio of 5.6525, above MK1's rank-4 health median of 4.23 (ancient-hp pass; one boss, one kill).

values.zone: Nightmare, Outskirts of Inoya, zone level 170

measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_hp_follows_rank_table'] stays None: this row carries `confounds`, so it decides no hypothesis. Its ratio, 5.6525, is 1.336 times RANK_TABLE[4].hp = 4.23, which is the feature's effect on this boss, not evidence that a boss's health does or does not follow the rank table.
confounds: The Bosses control's 3-affix top-up (16 Multishot, 17 Treasure Gobbler, 25 Pyromaniac) was written on the same boss and built into the same health, so the rank was not the only thing changed.
One boss, one kill, one zone.
The spread of MK1's ordinary rank-1/rank-4 health pairs behind the 4.23 median is not recorded, so how far outside it 5.6525 sits is unknown.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not established: 5.6525 against RANK_TABLE[4].hp = 4.23 is one confounded sample (see `confounds`), recorded as the measured health of a raised, topped-up boss. Whether a boss scales on health differently from an ordinary monster stays open until a boss is measured at a forced rank with nothing else changed.

measurements.what: The rank the Bosses control wrote at the entry of EnemyRaritySettings on a boss was still there at its exit, after the game's own setup ran: Karp_King_obj 3 (rare) and 4 (ancient), Damien_obj, Uber_Damien_obj and Uber_Anubis_obj 4 (ancient), each entering at enemyRarity 1. With the control off and the sliders at 100% ancient, a Karp_King_obj stayed at 1 and the sliders counted it left alone. A readback of what the hook wrote, not of anything the game built from it.
measurements.model: force_boss_rank('rare') == 3 and force_boss_rank('ancient') == 4 for a rank-1 boss, and force_boss_rank('off') == 1.

measurements.what: Three more bosses raised to rank 4, health only, with no rank-1 spawn of the same boss to compare: Damien_obj 159,906,250, Uber_Damien_obj 1,306,210,937, Uber_Anubis_obj 4,451,343,750.
measurements.model: None: no ratio without a rank-1 base.
measurements.not_reproduced: No rank-1 base was measured for these three bosses, so there is no ratio to set a hypothesis with; the values are recorded for a later session to compare against.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj's damage at rank 1 and rank 4 (ancient-damage): not observed. Every damage-named variable printed as an unproven key read, never a proven one.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_damage_follows_rank_table'] stays None.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not observed: no damage value was read through a proven route. ForgePact#44's Live procedure 1b measures it.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj's XP at rank 1 and rank 4 (ancient-xp): not observed. killExperience and experience printed as unproven key reads; experienceColor read as a plain number but is a colour, unchanged.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_xp_follows_rank_table'] stays None.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not observed: no XP value was read through a proven route. ForgePact#44's Live procedure 1b measures it.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj's drop rank, the first DropItem argument at its death (ancient-drop-rank): not run, the instrument blind on a boss. With droptrace armed, neither the rank-1 nor the rank-4 Karp_King_obj death printed a DropItem line, so there is no rank-1 anchor. The rank-3 (rare) Karp_King_obj death printed one, first argument 3: uncontrolled, not evidence.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_drop_rank_reaches_dropitem'] stays None.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not run: without a DropItem line at a rank-1 boss's death the rank-3 line cannot show that the raise moved the argument. ForgePact#44's Live procedure 1b measures it.

measurements.what: Karp_King_obj's drops per kill (ancient-drops), counted as new lines in ForgePact's itemdrops.jsonl: not observed. The rank-1 and rank-4 kills, both with droptrace armed, added 0 lines each; an untraced rank-1 kill added 20 and the traced rank-3 kill 20, so the two zeros are not a count of the boss's drops. Why those two deaths dropped nothing is not established here.
measurements.model: Not modelled: the model carries no drop count.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not observed: one kill at each rank, and the two that matter dropped nothing at all.

measurements.what: The same session's control on an ordinary monster (drop-rank-control): a Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj the Monster Rarity sliders raised to rank 4 died with drop rank 4, the first DropItem argument, as MK2 says of every ordinary monster.
measurements.model: An ordinary monster's drop rank is its rank (MK2); the drop rank instrument sees a raised rank.

measurements.what: Live 1b: the identity control for damage (rank-damage-control). An ordinary Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj spawned at rank 1, then raised by the Monster Rarity sliders to rank 3 and to rank 4 (each with the sliders' affix top-up: 30, 6 at rank 3; 5, 12, 18 at rank 4), read through the same probe as the Karp King: the variable `damage` read 257, 360 and 515, x1.4008 and x2.0039, within the check's 10% of MK1's x1.53 and x1.90. So `damage` holds a monster's damage on this instrument.
measurements.model: Each ratio is within 10% of RANK_TABLE[rank].damage (rank 3: 0.916 of 1.53; rank 4: 1.055 of 1.90).

measurements.what: Live 1b: the identity control for XP (rank-xp-control), on MK15's three Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj spawns: `killExperience` read 221, 943 and 1387 (x4.2670, x6.2760) and `experience` 96, 410 and 603 (x4.2708, x6.2813), each within the check's 2% of MK1's x4.25 and x6.25. The check named `killExperience`.
measurements.model: Each ratio, of both variables, is within 2% of RANK_TABLE[rank].xp (4.25 and 6.25).

measurements.what: Live 1b: the same three Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj spawns' health (`enemy_hp`, through the proven getter), not a control: 35,475 at rank 1, 201,764 at rank 3 (x5.6875) and 188,460 at rank 4 (x5.3125), against MK1's medians x2.98 and x4.23. The rank-4 spawn read less than the rank-3 one.
measurements.model: None: one spawn per rank is not MK1's median, and this one is not monotone in rank.
measurements.not_reproduced: One spawn per rank, each with a different affix top-up (MK15), reads well above MK1's health medians and falls from rank 3 to rank 4. Recorded because it shows one ordinary monster's health at a forced rank can sit far from the median, which is why a single boss's health ratio (MK7, MK20) decides nothing.

measurements.what: Live 1b: the drop rank instrument's control (drop-rank-control), repeated: MK15's rank-4 Skeleton_Mage_Fire_obj died with `droptrace` armed and printed one DropItem line whose first argument was 4, as MK2 says of every ordinary monster.
measurements.model: An ordinary monster's drop rank is its rank (MK2), as MK14.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj, a boss, unraised (Bosses control off; the game's own setup traced at enemyRarity 1), on three spawns: max_hp 44,625,000 each (enemy_hp 44,604,656.89, 44,605,214.39 and 44,611,567.5, the hero already hitting it; largest gap 6,910.61), `damage` 217, `killExperience` 4,950 and `experience` 2,152 on every read; its traced death printed one DropItem line with first argument 1 (baseline-drop-trace pass), the anchor MK23 is compared with.
measurements.model: scaled(1, ...) returns these bases unchanged; MK20-MK22's rank-1 values are these.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj, a boss, raised to rank 4 by ForgePact's Bosses control with that control's 3-affix top-up (12 Fire Enchanted, 20 Punisher, 31 Antimagus): health 210,992,578 (max_hp) against 44,625,000 at rank 1 (MK19), a ratio of 4.7281, above MK1's rank-4 health median of 4.23 (ancient-hp pass: enemy_hp 210,980,848.512 against the largest rank-1 read 44,611,567.5, x4.7293, far past the gap). Live 1 read x5.6525 on the same boss with other affixes (MK7).
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_hp_follows_rank_table'] stays None: this row carries `confounds`, so it decides no hypothesis. Its ratio is 1.118 times RANK_TABLE[4].hp = 4.23.
confounds: The Bosses control's 3-affix top-up (12 Fire Enchanted, 20 Punisher, 31 Antimagus) was built into the same health, and the session has no health control: the identity control's own health did not follow MK1 (MK17).
Two sessions on the same boss read x5.6525 (MK7, other affixes) and x4.7281, so one sample's health ratio does not say how a boss scales.
One boss, one kill, one zone.
measurements.not_reproduced: Not established: a confounded sample (see `confounds`), recorded as the measured health of a raised, topped-up boss. What a boss's health does at a forced rank with nothing else changed stays open.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj, a boss, raised to rank 4 by the Bosses control (same spawn as MK20): its damage, the variable `damage` that MK15 proved, read 455 against 217 at rank 1 (MK19), a ratio of 2.0968 (ancient-damage pass). MK1's rank-4 damage median is x1.90; 2.0968 is 1.104 times that, just outside the 10% the identity control was held to. The control itself read x2.0039 at rank 4, and whether this boss's damage follows the row is not established.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_damage_follows_rank_table'] stays None: this row carries `confounds`, so it decides no hypothesis.
confounds: The Bosses control's 3-affix top-up (12 Fire Enchanted, 20 Punisher, 31 Antimagus) was not matched by the identity control's rank-4 top-up (5, 12, 18), so the control does not stand in for this boss's affixes.
The identity control itself read 8.4% below the table at rank 3 (x1.4008 against x1.53) and 5.5% above it at rank 4 (x2.0039 against x1.90), so its 10% is a wide window on this instrument.
The ratio, x2.0968 against x1.90, is 0.4% outside that 10% window, on one spawn.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj, a boss, raised to rank 4 by the Bosses control (same spawn as MK20): its XP, the variable `killExperience` that MK16 proved, read 30,940 against 4,950 at rank 1 (MK19), a ratio of 6.2505 (ancient-xp pass; `experience` 13,452 against 2,152, x6.2509). MK1's rank-4 XP is exactly x6.25, so this boss's XP followed the table's row.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_xp_follows_rank_table'] is True: the ratio is within MK16's 2% of RANK_TABLE[4].xp = 6.25.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj's drop rank, the first DropItem argument at its death (ancient-drop-rank pass): 1 at the unraised boss's traced death (MK19's anchor), 4 at the traced death of the boss the Bosses control raised to rank 4 (same spawn as MK20). No DropItemBoss line was printed at either death.
measurements.model: HYPOTHESES['boss_drop_rank_reaches_dropitem'] is True: the first argument at the raised boss's death is the rank written, and the unraised boss's was 1.

measurements.what: Live 1b: Karp_King_obj's drops per kill (ancient-drops), as new lines in ForgePact's itemdrops.jsonl, with the research build's dropstats counters beside them (boss-drop-routine): the unraised boss's traced kill added 10 lines, the rank-4 boss's traced kill 12; one kill each. The untraced control kill added none and moved no counter; three other kills moved counters (two of them rank 4 by oset, not by the Bosses control). ItemBoss, BossGems and BossRunes stayed 0 at every kill.
measurements.model: Not modelled: the model carries no drop count.
measurements.not_reproduced: One kill per rank, and the hero's own attacks killed nearby monsters between reads, so a counter delta can include a death that was not the boss's. 10 against 12 lines is recorded, never a verdict on whether a raised boss drops more.
